practices.practice: Read the Azure DocumentDB connection string at runtime (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit connection strings/primary keys to source control or logs.
practices.source_name: Use LangChain on Azure with Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Use LangChain on Azure with Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Always use TLS in the Mongo connection string (mongodb+srv, tls=true) and reject insecure certificate validation in production.
practices.source_name: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID (Get cluster credentials)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB tls=true mongodb+srv connection best practices

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (managed identity) + RBAC or short-lived tokens for apps instead of embedding long-lived DB passwords; create least-privilege secondary users when needed.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer retrieving database credentials from a secret-store (Azure Key Vault or Managed Identity) at runtime rather than placing long-lived secrets in environment variables or files.
practices.source_name: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID (Get cluster credentials)
practices.how_found: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID

practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient/driver instance per process (singleton) and do not open a new client per request; initialize the client outside request/handler scope.
practices.prior_belief: Reuse pooled connections instead of opening a new client per request: configure driver pool settings (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS) and create one global client/Beanie motor client per process.

practices.practice: Tune connection-pool and timeout settings according to runtime context (serverless: small pools, short maxIdleTimeMS; long-running servers: larger pools and pre-warmed minPoolSize); initialize clients outside handlers.

Use the documented recommended connection options (mongodb+srv scheme when appropriate, tls=true, recommended authMechanism for Entra, retryWrites and maxIdleTimeMS values as documented) obtained from the cluster's Connection strings pane rather than constructing custom URIs from memory.
practices.source_name: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID (Get cluster credentials)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB connection string recommended options

practices.practice: Normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity and record the embedding model name and embedding dimensionality alongside the stored vector.
practices.prior_belief: When performing similarity search, normalize vectors before choosing a metric: if using cosine distance normalize vectors and then use inner-product/Euclidean depending on the engine; document which metric aligns to your embeddings.

practices.practice: Store embeddings as a numeric array (number[]) field; only number[] vectors are indexable by the DocumentDB vector engine.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index numeric array requirement

practices.practice: Create a dedicated cosmosSearch vector index with the correct kind (vector-diskann / vector-hnsw / vector-ivf), dimensions and similarity metric instead of treating vectors as ordinary fields.
practices.prior_belief: For similarity search, store embeddings as a fixed-length numeric array field (not a blob/string) and create a dedicated vector index with the correct dimension and distance metric (e.g., cosine or euclidean) rather than treating vectors as ordinary fields.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index best practices

practices.practice: When building vector indexes, explicitly configure and document algorithm hyperparameters (DiskANN: maxDegree, lBuild/lSearch; HNSW: m, efConstruction/efSearch; IVF: numLists) to match scale and recall/latency trade-offs.
practices.prior_belief: When creating vector indexes (HNSW / DiskANN /IVF), explicitly configure index hyperparameters (dimension, M / efConstruction / efSearch, metric) appropriate for your vector dimension and recall/latency tradeoffs and document that configuration in code.

practices.practice: Use the DocumentDB first-class search path: create search indexes via createSearchIndexes and query with the $search aggregation stage (textSearch/cosmosSearch) instead of the community $text operator.

When running vector kNN queries, apply server-side pre_filters (filter on metadata) and create conventional indexes on those filterable properties so filtering happens inside the cosmosSearch candidate stage rather than after KNN.
practices.source_name: Use LangChain on Azure with Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB pre_filter cosmosSearch pre-filter guidance

practices.practice: Keep documents well under the 16 MB BSON limit: put very large raw complaint text in blob storage or chunk long texts and store per-chunk embeddings to avoid oversized documents and to improve search performance.
practices.prior_belief: Keep documents reasonably small: if complaint text is large, either store raw text in a separate blob store and keep a truncated version in the document or chunk long texts and store embeddings per chunk to avoid hitting document size limits and to improve search performance.

practices.practice: Create conventional single-field or compound indexes for fields used in filters and aggregations (e.g., product_category, root_cause, urgency, created_at) before running production aggregations.
practices.prior_belief: Create conventional indexes for fields used in filters/joins/aggregations (e.g., category, root_cause, urgency_tier, created_at) before running production queries so aggregations and lookups use indexes.

practices.practice: Make index-creation idempotent: run createIndex/createSearchIndexes with stable specs and handle 'index already exists' or use hide→drop lifecycle so deployment scripts can be safely re-run.
practices.prior_belief: Define indexes (and index-creation helpers/scripts) to be idempotent: use createIndex with the same index spec and handle 'index already exists' errors gracefully so deploy scripts are safe to re-run.

practices.practice: Compute complaint hotspots server-side using aggregation pipelines ($group, $sort, $limit, $bucket) instead of pulling documents into the application, and ensure grouping fields are indexed.
practices.prior_belief: Use aggregation pipelines on the server (e.g., $group, $sort, $limit, $bucket) to compute complaint hotspots by category rather than pulling all documents into the app; ensure grouping fields are indexed to optimize the aggregation.

practices.practice: When seeding data, use bulk insert/batch or insertMany with unordered operations (ordered:false) or upserts to improve throughput and make the script idempotent; handle duplicate-key errors gracefully.
practices.prior_belief: Use bulk writes (insert_many / bulk_write) with unordered operations when seeding to improve throughput; handle duplicate-key errors and be idempotent so seed scripts can be re-run safely.
practices.source_name: Insert data into Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (insertMany guidance)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB insertMany unordered performance insert_many ordered:false

practices.practice: For local development with the DocumentDB Gateway container, connect on port 10260 with TLS and SCRAM-SHA-256 and drive relaxation of TLS from environment variables only; do not default tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true in code.

Verify the MongoDB driver you use supports the cluster's advertised MongoDB wire protocol version (Azure DocumentDB supports wire protocol versions 5.0–8.0); upgrade the driver if needed to match the server version.
practices.prior_belief: Ensure the MongoDB driver version is compatible with the server wire protocol (use a driver that supports MongoDB 7.0 when the cluster advertises MongoDB 7.0).
practices.source_name: Azure DocumentDB at a glance / MongoDB compatibility
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB MongoDB wire protocol versions supported 5.0 6.0 7.0 8.0

practices.practice: Define explicit Pydantic/Beanie document models with typed fields (and example schemaVersion) and use those models across the app rather than raw dicts to keep schemas consistent.
practices.prior_belief: Define clear Pydantic/Beanie models for documents (explicit fields, types, and index definitions) and use those models everywhere rather than raw dicts to keep schema consistent.

practices.practice: Pick shard/partition keys with high cardinality or use hashed shard keys; avoid low-cardinality fields (like simple 'category') as the primary shard key to prevent hot partitions.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid low-cardinality fields as shard/partition keys (e.g., 'category' may be too low-cardinality); choose a high-cardinality partition key or use hashed keys to distribute load evenly for large collections.

practices.practice: Monitor throughput and resource metrics and scale compute tier (and use Premium SSD v2 where appropriate) to meet IOPS/latency needs; size compute for throughput and use autoscale when available for production workloads.
practices.prior_belief: If the cluster exposes configurable throughput or instance sizes, monitor and scale provisioned resources (compute tier, RU/s or instance size) to meet latency/throughput needs, and use autoscale where available for production workloads.

practices.practice: Limit the number of nearest-neighbor results returned (k) and page results; avoid client-side scanning of the whole collection for similarity search.
practices.prior_belief: Limit the number of results returned from similarity queries (k) and paginate results; avoid scanning the whole collection in the application layer for nearest-neighbor search.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector-search k parameter and lSearch guidance

practices.practice: Use partial or sparse indexes for fields that are frequently missing (e.g., processed_flag, urgency) to reduce index size and write overhead when queries filter on those fields.
practices.prior_belief: Use partial or sparse indexes for fields that are often missing (e.g., processed_flag, urgency_tier) to reduce index size and improve write performance if queries filter on those fields.

practices.practice: Protect PII: use service-managed or customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest and consider client-side field-level encryption for highly sensitive fields.
practices.prior_belief: Protect PII by encrypting sensitive fields at rest (use Azure-managed encryption or customer-managed keys) and consider client-side field-level encryption for highly sensitive data.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB CMK data encryption guidance

practices.practice: Use semantic caching / a semantic cache pattern (cache embeddings and prior classification results keyed by a text hash) to avoid repeating expensive LLM and embedding calls for identical or near-duplicate texts.
practices.prior_belief: Cache embeddings and classification results for identical or near-duplicate complaint texts to avoid repeated LLM/embedding calls; store cache keys (e.g., text hash) alongside documents or in a separate cache store.
practices.source_name: Use LangChain on Azure with Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logging, analyze logs in Log Analytics, and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/storage/connection saturation and high vector-index memory usage.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and monitor slow queries and index usage (profiling or APM); add alerts for high latency, high error-rate operations, and high memory usage of vector indexes.

practices.practice: Keep dev/test operations safe: run unit tests against local or test clusters (Gateway container or test DB), never run destructive test seeds against production, and require explicit flags/confirmation for seed scripts.
practices.prior_belief: Keep deployment and test workflows safe: unit tests should use a local or test database and never run destructive write operations against a production cluster; seed scripts should be guarded and require an explicit flag/confirmation.

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network errors, and distinguish idempotent from non-idempotent operations (only auto-retry idempotent operations or use transactional boundaries for non-idempotent ones).
practices.prior_belief: Implement retry with exponential backoff for transient network failures; distinguish idempotent vs non-idempotent operations and only auto-retry idempotent operations (or use transaction boundaries / two-phase updates for non-idempotent ones).

practices.practice: Prefer the native AsyncPy driver where recommended (PyMongo's AsyncMongoClient) for new Python async code rather than Motor, because Motor is deprecated for new async code paths.

When creating vector indexes for large corpora prefer DiskANN (M30+), use HNSW for mid-size datasets and IVF for small demos; a single vector path supports only one index and vectors above the engine limits require product quantization/half-precision.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index type guidance (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF)
